title: ModuleScript
summary: A reusable code container that returns a value when loaded with require(). The backbone of organized Roblox projects: shared utilities, singletons, classes, and config all live in modules.

properties.name: Source
properties.description: The module's Luau code, editable via Studio or the API (server only for protected contexts).

properties.name: LinkedSource
properties.description: Optional asset reference to shared module code.

details.heading: Execution model
details.body: A ModuleScript's code runs exactly once per runtime (once on the server, once on the client if both require it) — the first time it is required. The returned value is cached; later requires return the cached value instantly without re-running the code.

details.heading: Return value
details.body: Whatever the top-level `return` produces is what require() gives back. With no return, require() yields `true`. A module can return a table, function, number — anything.

details.heading: Where they can live
details.body: Anywhere, but placement controls access: ReplicatedStorage/ReplicatedFirst are visible to both sides; ServerStorage/ServerScriptService are server-only; StarterPlayer/StarterGui areas are client-reachable.

details.heading: Circular requires
details.body: If module A requires B and B requires A (directly or transitively), Luau errors rather than deadlocking.

explanation.whatItIs: A script whose job is to be *loaded*, not to run on its own. It holds reusable code — and hands it to whoever asks via require().
explanation.whyItExists: Copy-pasting the same helper across ten Scripts is how projects die. ModuleScripts give code one home, one name, and many users.
whenToUse: Shared helpers both client and server need (ReplicatedStorage)
Singletons: one state object every script on a side shares
whenNotToUse: As a replacement for Scripts/LocalScripts — modules don't run until required
For one-shot game logic that belongs in a Script
For server secrets in a client-visible location — anything clients can require, exploiters can read
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
ModuleScript
     ↓
require()
     ↓
module runs / loads        (once per runtime)
     ↓
return value
     ↓
your variable receives it  (same value every time)
```
tips: require(WaitForChild("ModuleName")) on the client — replication timing matters
Modules are the unit of architecture: name them after their one responsibility
Keep requires acyclic and one-directional (features → utilities, never the reverse)
commonMistakes: Forgetting `return` — require() then gives `true`, and `true.DoThing()` errors 'attempt to index boolean'
Expecting the module to re-run per require — it's cached
Confusing the ModuleScript Instance (the object in the tree) with the value it returns
Client requiring a module in ServerStorage — impossible; it isn't replicated
Doing slow initialization in the module body — it blocks every first requirer

examples.title: The classic module + require
examples.code:
-- == ReplicatedStorage/Greeter (ModuleScript) ==
local Greeter = {}

function Greeter.hello(name)
    return "Hello, " .. name .. "!"
end

return Greeter

-- == Any Script or LocalScript ==
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Greeter = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Greeter"))

print(Greeter.hello("Raanis"))   --> Hello, Raanis!
examples.whyItWorks: require() runs the module once and returns its table. Every script that requires Greeter gets the same table — one definition, many users.

examples.title: Module as shared config
examples.code:
-- == ReplicatedStorage/GameConfig (ModuleScript) ==
return {
    RoundLength = 120,
    MaxPlayers = 12,
    CoinValue = 5,
}

-- Server Script:
local config = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.GameConfig)
print(config.RoundLength)   --> 120
-- Client sees the same numbers — single source of truth.
